title: Cost Segregation + MASS: Turn Idle Land Into Revenue and Year-One Tax Savings
summary: Learn how pairing MASS relocatable storage units with cost segregation can add rentable space fast and speed up tax deductions on your self-storage facility.
body_markdown:
Most self-storage owners think about upgrades in terms of what they cost. The smartest owners also ask a second question: how fast can this project pay me back?


That's where two tools from the Janus R3 Program work best together. MASS (Movable Additional Storage Structures) turns unused land into rentable units quickly. Cost segregation helps you recover the cost of improvements much faster through depreciation. Used together, they can improve both sides of your balance sheet: more revenue coming in and less tax going out. And acting quickly could save you big on your 2026 tax return.


## What is R3?


R3 (Restore, Rebuild, Replace) is the Janus International program for reinvesting in existing self-storage facilities. Instead of buying more land or building from scratch, R3 helps owners get more from the footprint they already have.


- **Restore:** Paving, painting, building repairs and exterior upgrades that protect asset value.
- **Rebuild:** Unit remixes, office remodels and MASS additions that match your space to current demand.
- **Replace:** Door replacements, hallway reskins and security upgrades that cut maintenance and improve reliability.


MASS and cost segregation sit at the center of the Rebuild and Replace strategies.


## MASS: New revenue from land you already own


Got an empty corner of the lot, unused parking spaces or an odd-shaped parcel? MASS units are fully steel, drive-up relocatable storage units built to match the look and function of traditional self-storage.


Why owners choose MASS:


- **Fast to add.** Units can be delivered and set without a long construction timeline, so they start earning sooner.
- **Same tenant experience.** Full-size roll-up doors and standard self-storage materials mean units blend in with the rest of your facility.
- **Flexible.** Units can be moved with a forklift if your site plan changes.
- **Often easier to permit.** MASS units are frequently allowed where permanent buildings or shipping containers are not.
- **Classifed as equipment.** This is the big one for taxes, and we'll explain why below.


## Cost segregation: Stop waiting 39 years for your deductions


Under standard straight-line depreciation, a commercial building is written off over 39 years. That means most of the money you put into your facility comes back to you very slowly.


A[cost segregation](https://www.janusintl.com/the-complete-guide-to-self-storage-renovations-and-cost-segregation) study is an engineering-based analysis that breaks your property into its individual parts and moves eligible items into shorter recovery periods: 5, 7 or 15 years


instead of 39.


Self-storage is especially well suited to this because so much of a facility is made up of paving, fencing, gates, lighting, security systems, partitions and roll-up doors, not just the building shell.


For self-storage owners, cost segregation can help in 3 ways:


1. Faster depreciation on your existing facility.


Components already on your property may qualify for shorter lives, even if you bought the facility years ago (through a look-back study).


2. Write-offs on what you remove.


When you replace old doors or partitions, a partial asset disposition can let you write off the remaining undepreciated value of the items you tear out, instead of depreciating doors that no longer exist.


3. Faster recovery on what you add.


New doors, MASS units and other qualifying upgrades can be depreciated on accelerated schedules.


## Why MASS and cost segregation are a strong pair


Because[MASS units](https://www.janusintl.com/products/relocatable-storage-mass) are classified as equipment, not real property, they can qualify for accelerated tax treatment that a permanent building can't.


Under current federal tax law:


• 100% bonus depreciation is now permanent


for qualifying property acquired and placed in service after January 19, 2025. That means eligible assets can be fully deducted in the first year.


• Section 179 expensing


allows up to $2,560,000 in qualifying purchases to be deducted in 2026, with a phase-out starting at $4,090,000. (Section 179 deductions can't exceed your business's taxable income; bonus depreciation doesn't have that limit.)


In plain terms: a MASS addition can start generating rental income quickly and may be fully deductible in the year it's placed in service. That combination can shorten your payback period dramatically.


## Real results: SPMI in San Antonio


[SPMI turned unused space at its San Antonio facility into Class A MASS units](https://www.janusintl.com/becoming-a-total-smart-storage-solution) . The results:


• About $78,240 per year


in added revenue from 50 former parking spaces
• Roughly $1.12 million


in added facility value at a 7% cap rate
• About $300,000 saved in taxes


through cost segregation


That's the R3 approach in action: new revenue from existing land, more asset value and a faster return on the investment.


## Why added income matters for asset value


Every dollar of new net operating income (NOI) raises what your facility is worth. At a 7% cap rate, each $100,000 in added annual NOI adds roughly $1.43 million in facility value. When cost segregation also lowers the after-tax cost of the project, your return on that investment improves even more.


## Why talk to us before year-end


To claim a deduction on your 2026 tax return, qualifying property generally has to be placed in service by December 31, not just ordered. If you're weighing a MASS addition or door replacement, now is the time to:


1. Get a facility assessment


to find idle land, slow-renting unit sizes and worn doors.
2. Request a free preliminary cost segregation review


. Janus works with cost segregation experts who can estimate what your facility may qualify for.
3. Talk to your CPA


about timing, Section 179 versus bonus depreciation, and your look-back options.


Even if a project lands in 2027, planning now puts you first in line for spring rental season.


[Read our Cost Segregation Guide](https://www.janusintl.com/the-complete-guide-to-self-storage-renovations-and-cost-segregation) to discover how reclassifying portions of your building and improvements may help accelerate depreciation and generate significant tax savings.
